title: Strength-reduced slope response
interpretation: A controlled small-strain numerical response to a prescribed strength reduction. This is not a complete landslide, calibrated site prediction, native MAT173 validation, or general solver-equivalence result.

source.mat173_branch: constant-property, no-joint Mohr-Coulomb, NOVOID=1 selected; six principal stress planes; nonassociated dilation

run.initial_condition: zero stress; gravity ramped over 0.02 s; numerical damping 0.995 applied to velocity and affine C during balancing only, then removed

render.surface_method: Build hexahedral cells only when all 8 corners are original neighboring material points from the initial regular x-y-z lattice. vtkGeometryFilter extracts the connected exterior faces; no new coordinates are added. Partial boundary cells are omitted, so the connected boundary is inset by up to one particle spacing.
render.scalar_method: Equivalent plastic strain is read from original MAT173 particle history and linearly interpolated over connected exterior cells. No scalar smoothing, clipping, or rescaling is applied.

limitations: MAT173 delivery manifest reports complex_final_check_status=NOT_VALIDATED and delivery_complete=false; material-specific native activation and history mapping remain pending.
The JAX adapter is a selected-branch small-strain return map driven by corotated logarithmic strain increments; finite-deformation host spin and native history semantics are not validated.
The calculation starts from zero stress, not measured or geostatically initialized stresses; the pre-trigger equilibrium is produced by a recorded damped gravity-settling procedure.
The finite slope has no pore pressure, water table, joints, erosion, progressive weakening, or site calibration.

Most downslope COM projection at termination comes from vertical settlement; plasticity is broad rather than a narrow basal shear band. The run stops at the small-strain limit and does not demonstrate full landslide runout.

The direct Fortran/JAX point comparison covers one fixed-axis, normal-strain two-generator symmetric edge return only; it does not test shear, face, apex, NOVOID tension, general finite strain, native UMAT mapping, or complex Final Check.
